spots.summary: The Wawel Royal Castle and the Wawel Hill on which it sits constitute the most historically and culturally significant site in Poland.

spots.name: Main Square, Kraków

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Main Market Square a historic square located in the Old Town of Kraków, Poland.

spots.name: Kraków Old Town
spots.summary: Old Town is the oldest, historic part of the city of Kraków within the Planty Park, Poland.

spots.name: St. Mary's Basilica in Kraków
spots.summary: The Basilica of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary, known colloquially as the St. Mary's Basilica, is a historic Roman Catholic parish church located at Mariacki Square at the north-eastern corner of the Main Market Square in the Old Town of Kraków, Poland.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Basilica of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary, Kraków

spots.name: Wawel Cathedral
spots.summary: The Archcathedral Basilica of Saint Stanislaus and Saint Wenceslaus, known colloquially as Wawel Cathedral, is a Catholic cathedral situated on Wawel Hill in Kraków, Poland. Nearly 1,000 years old, it is part of the Wawel Castle Complex and is a national sanctuary which served as the coronation site of Polish monarchs.

spots.name: Wawel
spots.summary: The Wawel Royal Castle and the Wawel Hill on which it sits constitute the most historically and culturally significant site in Poland.

spots.name: Veit Stoss altarpiece in Kraków
spots.summary: The Altarpiece by Veit Stoss, also St. Mary's Altar, is a large Gothic altarpiece and a national treasure of Poland. It is located behind the high altar of St. Mary's Basilica in the city of Kraków.

spots.name: Rakowice Cemetery
spots.summary: Rakowice Cemetery is a historic necropolis and a cultural heritage monument located at 26 Rakowicka Street in Warszawskie, the former district of Kraków, Poland.

spots.name: Sukiennice
spots.summary: The Cloth Hall, is a historic cloth hall located in the centre of the Main Market Square in Old Town of Kraków, Poland.

spots.name: Czartoryski Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Princes Czartoryski Museum – often abbreviated to Czartoryski Museum – is a historic museum in Kraków, Poland, and one of the country's oldest museums. The initial collection was formed in 1796 in Puławy by Princess Izabela Czartoryska. The Museum officially opened in 1878.

spots.name: Adam Mickiewicz Monument
spots.summary: Adam Mickiewicz Monument, a bronze monument located in the Main Market Square in the Old Town of Kraków, Poland.

spots.name: Polish Aviation Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Polish Aviation Museum is a large museum of historic aircraft and aircraft engines in Kraków, Poland. It is located at the site of the no-longer functional Kraków-Rakowice-Czyżyny Airport. This airfield, established by Austria-Hungary in 1912, is one of the oldest in the world.

spots.name: Kraków Ghetto
spots.summary: The Kraków Ghetto, officially named the Jewish Residential District in Krakow, was one of five major metropolitan Nazi ghettos created by Germany in the new General Government territory during the German occupation of Poland in World War II.

spots.name: Sigismund's Chapel

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Sigismund's Chapel is a royal chapel of the Wawel Cathedral in Kraków, Poland. Built as a funerary chapel for the last members of the Jagiellonian Dynasty, it has been hailed by many art historians as "the most beautiful example of the Tuscan Renaissance north of the Alps".

spots.name: Kazimierz
spots.summary: Kazimierz was historically a city and is now a district incorporated into Kraków, Poland. Until 1954 the VIII quarter of the city, it is now part of the District I Old Town.

spots.name: St. Adalbert's church
spots.summary: The Church of St. Adalbert or the Church of St. Wojciech, located on the intersection of the Main Market Square and Grodzka Street in Old Town, Kraków, is one of the oldest stone churches in Poland.

spots.name: Rynek Underground
spots.summary: The Rynek Underground museum of Kraków is situated below the market square of the city. The museum is approximately 4000 square meters in size.

spots.name: Saints Peter and Paul Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of Saints Apostles Peter and Paul is a historic Roman Catholic Polish Baroque church located at 52a Grodzka Street in the Old Town of Kraków, Poland.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of Saints Apostles Peter and Paul, Kraków

spots.name: Kraków Barbican
spots.summary: The Barbican is a barbican – a fortified outpost once connected to the city walls. It is a historic gateway leading into the Old Town of Kraków, Poland.

spots.name: Royal Tombs of the Wawel Cathedral
Wawel Dragon
spots.summary: Wawel Dragon Statue is a monument at the foot of the Wawel Hill in Kraków, Poland, in front of the Wawel Dragon's den, dedicated to the mythical Wawel Dragon. Installed in 1972, the statue is capable of letting out fire from its mouth on demand. Usually it does so every 15 minutes.

spots.name: Planty Park
spots.summary: Planty is a historic urban park surrounding the Old Town in Kraków, Poland. It was built on the site of the destroyed Medieval defensive walls of the city.

spots.name: Tomb of Casimir IV Jagiellon
spots.summary: The tomb of Casimir IV Jagiellon, located in Wawel Cathedral, Kraków, is a late 15th century masterpiece created in red marble by German sculptor Veit Stoss in the late Gothic style.

spots.name: St. Andrew's Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of St. Andrew is a historic Roman Catholic conventual church of the Order of Saint Clare located at 54 Grodzka Street in the Old Town of Kraków, Poland.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Corpus Christi Basilica

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Corpus Christi Church, is a historic Roman Catholic parish and conventual church of the Canons Regular of the Lateran located at 26 Bożego Ciała Street in Kazimierz, the former district of Kraków, Poland.

spots.name: Skałka

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of St. Michael the Archangel and St. Stanislaus Bishop and Martyr, known colloquially as the Church on the Rock and Small Rock is a historic Roman Catholic conventual church of the Order of Saint Paul the First Hermit located at 15 Skałeczna Street in Kazimierz, the former district of Kraków, Poland.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of St. Michael the Archangel and St. Stanislaus Bishop and Martyr, Kraków

spots.name: Town Hall Tower
spots.summary: Town Hall Tower is one of the main focal points of the Main Market Square in the Old Town of Kraków, Poland.

spots.name: Nowa Huta
spots.summary: Nowa Huta is the easternmost district of Kraków, Poland. With more than 200,000 inhabitants, it is one of the most populous areas of the city. Until 1990, the neighbouring districts were considered expansions of the original Nowa Huta district, and were linked by the same tramway system.

spots.name: Collegium Maius
spots.summary: The Collegium Maius located in Kraków Old Town, Poland, is the Jagiellonian University's oldest building, dating back to the 14th century. It stands at the corner of ulica Jagiellońska and ulica Świętej Anny near the Main Square of the historic city centre.

spots.name: Kościuszko's Mound
spots.summary: Kościuszko's Mound is an artificial mound in Kraków, Poland. It was erected by Cracovians in commemoration of the Polish national leader Tadeusz Kościuszko, and modelled after Kraków's prehistoric mounds of Krak and Wanda.

spots.name: Sukiennice Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Gallery of 19th-Century Polish Art at Sukiennice, is a division of the National Museum, Kraków, Poland. The gallery is housed on the upper floor of the Renaissance Sukiennice Cloth Hall in the center of the Main Market Square in Old Town Kraków.

spots.name: St. Leonard's Crypt
spots.summary: St. Leonard's Crypt under the Wawel Cathedral in Kraków, Poland, is a Romanesque crypt founded in the 11th century by Casimir I the Restorer who made Kraków his royal residence as the capital.

spots.name: Krakus' Mound
spots.summary: Krakus' Mound, also called Krak's Mound, is a tumulus located in the Podgórze district of Kraków, Poland, and is thought the resting place of Kraków's mythical founder, King Krakus.

spots.name: Church of the Holy Trinity, Kraków

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of the Holy Trinity, known colloquially as the Dominicans Church is a historic Roman Catholic conventual church of the Order of Preachers located at 12 Stolarska Street in the Old Town of Kraków, Poland.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of the Holy Trinity, Kraków (Old Town)

spots.name: Old Synagogue
spots.summary: The Old Synagogue was a former Orthodox Jewish congregation and fortress synagogue, located at 24 Szeroka Street, in the Kazimierz district of Kraków, in the Lesser Poland Voivodeship of Poland.

spots.name: Divine Mercy Sanctuary

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Divine Mercy Sanctuary in Kraków, Poland, is a Roman Catholic basilica dedicated to the devotion of the Divine Mercy, and is the resting place of Saint Faustina Kowalska.

spots.name: St. Florian's Gate
spots.summary: St. Florian's Gate in Kraków, Poland, is one of the best-known Polish Gothic towers, and a focal point of Kraków's Old Town.

spots.name: Church of St. Anne

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of St. Anne, is a historic Roman Catholic parish and university collegiate church located at 13 św. Anny Street in the Old Town of Kraków, Poland.

spots.name: Grunwald Monument
spots.summary: The Grunwald Monument is an equestrian statue of King of Poland Władysław II Jagiełło (1352–1434) located at Matejko Square in Kraków, Poland.

spots.name: Historic Centre of Kraków
spots.summary: The Historic Centre of Kraków is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Kraków, Poland.

spots.name: Juliusz Słowacki Theatre
spots.summary: Juliusz Słowacki Theatre is a historic, 19th-century Eclectic-style theatre and opera house located at 1 Świętego Ducha Square in the Old Town of Kraków, Poland, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

spots.name: Church of the Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Church of the Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary known colloquially as the Carmelites Church and Church in Piasek is a historic Roman Catholic parish and conventual church of the Carmelites located at 19 Karmelicka Street, in the former Piasek district of Kraków, Poland.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of the Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary, Kraków

spots.name: Kraków-Płaszów concentration camp
spots.summary: Płaszów, officially named Płaszów concentration camp near Kraków, was a German Nazi concentration camp operated by the SS in the area of Podgórze and Wola Duchacka near Płaszów, a southern suburb of Kraków, in the General Governorate of German-occupied Poland.

spots.name: St. Florian's Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of St. Florian, is a historic Roman Catholic parish, university collegiate church, and a Minor Basilica located at 2 Kurniki Street in Kleparz, the former district of Kraków, Poland.

spots.name: Wawel Royal Castle – State Art Collection

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Wawel Royal Castle – State Art Collection is the residence museum and collection housed in the historic Wawel Castle of Kraków. The collection was inaugurated officially in 1930, with its current name introduced in 1994.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Wawel Royal Castle – State Art Collection

spots.name: Floriańska Street
spots.summary: Floriańska Street is one of the main streets in Kraków Old Town and one of the most famous promenades in the city.

spots.name: National Museum in Kraków

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The National Museum in Kraków, popularly abbreviated as MNK, is the largest museum in Poland. Established in 1879, the museum consists of 21 departments which are divided by art period: 11 galleries, 2 libraries, and 12 conservation workshops.

spots.name: Museum of Kraków

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue

spots.summary: The Historical Museum of the City of Kraków in Kraków, Poland, was granted the status of an independent institution in 1945. Originally, it was a branch of the Old Records Office of Kraków, in operation from 1899.

spots.name: Remah Synagogue

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: The Remah Synagogue, is an Orthodox Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at 40 Szeroka Street, in the historic Kazimierz district of Kraków, in the Lesser Poland Voivodeship of Poland.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: National Bards crypt of the Wawel
spots.summary: National Bards crypt is a crypt located in the basements of the Wawel Cathedral on Wawel Hill. It serves as the burial place for Adam Mickiewicz and Juliusz Słowacki, two prominent poets of the Romantic era whose works have become an essential part of Polish culture.
spots.wikipediaTitle: National Bards crypt of the Wawel

spots.name: Camaldolese Priory, Kraków

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Camaldolese Hermit Monastery in Kraków is a Camaldolese priory in Bielany in Kraków, Poland. The monastery is located on the 326-metre (1,070 ft) Silver Mount. It consists of hermitages and the Assumption of Mary Church.

spots.name: Helena Modrzejewska National Old Theatre
spots.summary: The Helena Modrzejewska National Old Theatre a historic theater located at 5 Jagiellońska Street in the Old Town of Kraków, Poland.

spots.name: Piłsudski's Mound
spots.summary: Piłsudski's Mound located in Kraków, Poland, was constructed by the Polish people in honor of Józef Piłsudski.

spots.name: Grodzka Street
spots.summary: Grodzka Street – one of the oldest streets in Kraków, Poland. Grodzka was part of a former north–south trade route. The street is part of the Royal Route, used by Polish kings to reach Wawel Castle. The earliest documents referencing its name date from the thirteenth century.

spots.name: Tempel Synagogue

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Tempel Synagogue also Progressive Synagogue is a Reform Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at 24 Miodowa Street, in the historic Kazimierz district of Kraków, Poland.

spots.name: Dżok Monument
spots.summary: Dżok ("Jock") was a black mongrel dog who was seen waiting in vain for the entire year (1990–1991) at the Rondo Grunwaldzkie roundabout in Kraków, Poland, to be fetched back by his master, who had died there.

spots.summary: Built in 1618, this church was constructed in early baroque style for the Carmelichans. Later, it was used by the nuns of the hospital of the Holy Ghost.
